Laura / Marcus —

Draft answers below (technical + suggested RFP wording). I'm keeping the language concise for the RFP, with a short appendix for details. Please flag anything you want softened for legal.

1) Fields captured in audit logs (default hosted behavior):
- timestamp, request_id, account_id (customer-managed), api_key_id, model_id/version, endpoint/route, input_size_tokens, output_size_tokens, latency_ms, node_id, region, routing_decision, error_code (if any).
- NOTE: request/response payloads are not stored by default in hosted mode. Content logging (full prompt/response) is available only with explicit customer opt-in (for debugging) and will be called out in contract.

2) Export mechanisms:
- Admin Audit Log API: GET /v1/admin/audit-logs?start=YYYY-MM-DD&end=YYYY-MM-DD returns ndjson with gzip support.
- We support scheduled daily export to customer S3 buckets (s3://...) or SFTP via connector (credentials provided by customer). Exports are delivered as gzipped JSONL files named audit-YYYYMMDD.jsonl.gz.
- Rate limits: control-plane export endpoints are throttled; we recommend daily exports for full history. For ad-hoc exports we can provide time-windowed pulls (max 90-day window per request on hosted).

3) Retention windows (standard options):
- Hosted (default): 90 days retention for audit metadata.
- Hosted (enterprise add-on): configurable up to 7 years (archival storage) for customers who purchase compliance retention add-on.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): default 365 days; retention configurable per customer up to 7 years with archival option.
- Private / On-prem: retention controlled entirely by the customer; Redwood does not manage retention unless contracted to operate.

4) Deletion / proof:
- Hosted: customers may submit deletion requests for account-scoped logs; deletion from active stores occurs within 7 days of approved request and archival shards purged according to the retained policy. We provide an export and a deletion certificate (signed statement with export manifest) as evidence.
- Dedicated: on-premise deletion or retention policy changes can be executed via support; we commit to execution within 48 hours for on-prem and dedicated hosts under enterprise contract.
- Private: customer-managed — Redwood can provide guidance and scripts for secure wipe.

5) Evidence / compliance artifacts:
- SOC2 Type II report (redacted) available on NDA.
- Sample export: small NDJSON audit export (sanitized) provided for inspection.
- We can provide an export manifest and a cryptographic hash for delivered export files for verification.

Suggested RFP answer (concise):
"Redwood provides structured audit logs that include request metadata (timestamps, request IDs, account and API key identifiers, model/version, routing and latency metrics, and error codes). Audit metadata is retained by default for 90 days (hosted) and can be extended via enterprise add-ons or configured longer on Dedicated and Private deployments. We support daily automated exports to customer-owned S3 or SFTP endpoints and provide deletion certificates or manifests upon successful purges. Content-level logging (full prompts/responses) is disabled by default and is only enabled with explicit customer consent and contractual terms."

Attachments I will produce: short appendix (fields list), export sample (sanitized), and one-line API call examples.

— Stephanie
Principal Product Security Engineer

Hi Lisa — quick answers below. Tagging Marcus/Stephanie for technical confirmation.

1) Hosted deletion SLA / backups:
- Active stores: deletion from primary indices and active replicas is completed within 7 calendar days of approved request.
- Backups/archival shards: our standard backup retention cycle is 30 days for hot backups and up to 90 days for long-tail shards; we will purge customer data from backups within 30 days after the approved deletion request and provide a deletion certificate. If an accelerated purge is required for regulatory reasons, Redwood can negotiate an expedited removal SLA as part of an enterprise DPA (typical commitment: 15 days with contractual acceptance and proof-of-work artifact).

2) S3 export integrity & replication:
- We support per-file SHA256 hashes included in the export manifest; we can also sign manifests with our key for tamper-evidence.
- Cross-region replication: Redwood writes to the customer-provided S3 bucket. If the bucket has cross-region replication configured on the customer side, that will apply. For customers who require Redwood-managed replication, we can support delivering copies to two region buckets as part of an enterprise delivery add-on.

If you'd like, we can add the accelerated purge and multi-region delivery options into the commercial proposal.

Best,
Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
